solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Skill in writing story books

parts.note: a written story is a tale
NT, the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A remark on a novelist's gift: skill shown in writing storybooks.
explanation.definitionFit: A talent is a natural gift or aptitude, a synonym for skill.

clue.text: Ted was after Greta, perhaps, identified as a victim

indicators.note: was after places one piece behind the other in the answer
perhaps suggests the name Greta could be some other arrangement of its letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Ted chased Greta, it seems, and she was singled out as his prey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' looks like doubt about Greta, but signals an anagram; 'was after' sets Ted at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To be targeted is to be picked out for attack, as a victim is chosen.

clue.text: Instructor is oddly curt, intercepting a sexy look

indicators.note: intercepting means one piece breaks into the middle of the other, cutting it open

parts.note: a leer is a lascivious look

indicators.note: oddly signals the word curt is set out in a strange order

explanation.surface: A teacher behaves strangely brusquely while blocking a lustful glance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' tempts you to take alternate letters of curt, but here it shuffles them (CTUR), and 'intercepting' splits the leer around them.
explanation.definitionFit: A university lecturer is a teacher, someone who instructs students.

clue.text: They get knocked down in alleys

definitions.text: They get knocked down in alleys

parts.words: They get knocked down in alleys
parts.note: suggests victims of street muggings, but means the skittles set up in a bowling or skittle alley

explanation.surface: People attacked and floored in back lanes.
explanation.walkthrough: Alleys here are skittle alleys; the nine skittles are knocked over by a thrown ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninepins are the wooden skittles in the old game of skittles, set up to be bowled over.

clue.text: Adore old novel featuring a fabulous city

indicators.note: novel means new, so these words appear in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A reader loves an old novel set in a legendary city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book, but signals a new order of ADORE OLD.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary city of gold sought by Spanish explorers in South America existed only in fable.

clue.text: People living around pubs

definitions.meaning: in Britain, the local is one's neighbourhood public house

explanation.surface: Residents who live near the bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Locals are nearby residents, and a local is also the British name for one's regular nearby pub.

clue.text: Experts know them to be edible bulbs

definitions.meaning: from the idiom 'to know one's ...', meaning to be an expert
vegetables grown as bulbs and eaten

explanation.surface: Specialists can recognise which bulbs are safe to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom 'know your onions' means to be expert, and the vegetable is an edible bulb.

clue.text: Cram everything in the night before? On the contrary for this exam

indicators.note: cram means stuff one thing inside another
in says where the stuffed piece goes, within the other
on the contrary reverses the container: the night before goes inside everything, not the other way round

parts.note: all means everything
eve is the evening before an event

explanation.surface: Advice against cramming everything the night before an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as study advice, but 'Cram ... in' is a container and 'On the contrary' swaps which piece holds which. An A level is the British advanced exam taken at about 18.
explanation.definitionFit: The A level is the advanced school examination in England and Wales, the kind of test students cram for.

clue.text: More than right, but stupid

definitions.meaning: an angle greater than a right angle

explanation.surface: Someone overcorrect yet dim.
explanation.definitionFit: An obtuse angle exceeds ninety degrees, and an obtuse person is slow-witted.

clue.text: Telephone about an account — for betting?

indicators.note: about means one word goes around another

parts.note: to ring someone is to telephone them
AC is the abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: Phone up about an account, perhaps a bookmaker's.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse racing is the sport most associated with placing bets.

clue.text: Bill takes detectives to hospital department after crash

indicators.note: takes means the first piece is followed by the next
to joins the next piece on at the end

parts.note: AC, short for account, which is a bill
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police
ENT, the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A policeman named Bill brings detectives to the hospital after a car crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a person's name (Old Bill is slang for the police) but is the account abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An accident, as on the road, is a crash or collision.

clue.text: Provides some point to jokes

parts.note: E, east, a compass point
quips are witty remarks

explanation.surface: Supplies a bit of edge to a comedian's lines.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip is to furnish or supply with what is needed.

clue.text: Let banks arrange covers for retirement

indicators.note: arrange means the letters of these words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Allow the banks to set up pension cover for old age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' suggests a pension, but means going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedding covers used when retiring for the night are woollen blankets.

clue.text: Home fixture for City, but needs to be arranged

parts.note: Bath is a city in Somerset, England

indicators.note: the word but must be put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A football team's home match against City needs organising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs to be arranged' turns BUT into TUB. 'Home fixture' looks like a football match, but is a fitting in a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A bath is fitted permanently in a house, a fixed piece of household plumbing.

clue.text: Used for lighting and heating in Madagascar

indicators.note: in shows the answer sits within the letters of the island's name

explanation.surface: A fuel used for lights and warmth on Madagascar.
explanation.definitionFit: Town gas and natural gas fuel lamps and heaters.

clue.text: It's all off!

parts.note: sounds like a cancellation, but is the stage direction sending every actor off stage

explanation.surface: An announcement that the plan is cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin stage direction means 'they go out', telling all the actors to leave the stage.

clue.text: Salt found in the mustard

indicators.note: found in tells us the letters are within the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: Salt discovered in the mustard pot.
explanation.walkthrough: Salt is the condiment on the surface, but an old sailor in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tar and salt are both old slang for a sailor.

clue.text: Was no faster?

parts.note: seems to ask about speed, but means someone who was not fasting, so took food

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone was any quicker.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is not a faster, going without food, has dined.

clue.text: Bags wild she-cats

indicators.note: wild means the letters of the hyphenated word run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone captures feral female cats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bags' looks like a verb meaning catches, but is a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Sachets are small sealed packets or bags.

clue.text: Extra comment following school game shows spirit

indicators.note: following places the extra comment after the other pieces

parts.note: nap is a card game, short for Napoleon
PS, a postscript added to a letter

explanation.surface: A postscript after a school match shows team spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' suggests morale but means a strong drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Schnapps is a strong alcoholic spirit.

clue.text: Seeking help concerning a series of lectures

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a course is a programme of lectures

explanation.surface: Asking for help with a lecture series.
explanation.definitionFit: Recourse is the act of turning to someone or something for assistance.

clue.text: Mean sailor upset students' game

parts.note: base means mean or low

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: AB, an able seaman
L is a learner, so two learners give LL

explanation.surface: A spiteful sailor wrecked the students' match.
explanation.definitionFit: Baseball is the American bat-and-ball sport.

clue.text: Spots city maze complex

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London

indicators.note: complex means intricate, signalling a tangled arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone notices an urban maze complex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' turns EC plus MAZE into ECZEMA. 'Spots' looks like a verb but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Eczema is a skin condition producing itchy patches and rashes.

clue.text: Revised a programme, giving Edward a new diet

parts.note: Ed is short for Edward

indicators.note: new means the letters of diet are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A TV show was reworked to give Edward a new eating plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Editing a broadcast means cutting and correcting it before transmission.

clue.text: Cards that make one laugh

definitions.meaning: the wild playing cards added to a pack
people who tell jokes and amuse others

explanation.surface: Greeting cards that amuse.
explanation.definitionFit: The extra wild cards in a pack bear a jester, and comedians who amuse people are wags.

clue.text: Goes around in women's clothes

definitions.meaning: travels round the edge of something
garments hanging from the waist worn by women

explanation.surface: Someone wanders about wearing women's dresses.
explanation.definitionFit: To skirt is to pass around the edge, and skirts are women's garments.

clue.text: Potting aid

parts.note: seems to be a gardening tool, but means the stick used to pot balls in snooker or pool

explanation.surface: A tool for planting in pots.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker, the stick used to strike balls into pockets helps the player pot them.

clue.text: Join a small company in this place

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
here means in this place

explanation.surface: An invitation to join a small firm based right here.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere is to stick together, to unite as one.

clue.text: It may have to be turned before making an entry

definitions.text: It may have to be turned before making an entry

parts.words: It may have to be turned before making an entry
parts.note: sounds like a page or an account record, but means a handle turned to open a door

explanation.surface: Something like a page turned before writing in a diary.
explanation.definitionFit: A round door handle is twisted to open the door and go in.

clue.text: Ruined, but not executed

explanation.surface: A condemned man saved from the gallows but still ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: Undone means ruined, and also means a task left not done.

clue.text: Conjectures will appear if he is accepted by the Conservatives

indicators.note: accepted by means taken in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: Tories are members of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Speculation will arise if a man is taken on by the Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Theories are hypotheses or ideas not yet proved, like speculations.

clue.text: City may be seen as part of Ancient Greece

definitions.text: City may be seen as part of Ancient Greece

indicators.note: may be seen loosely suggests the words can be viewed as something else, rearranged

explanation.surface: A city regarded as part of the ancient Greek world.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the city; within it, 'may be seen' loosely signals that 'as part' be rearranged. 'as part' looks like it hides the city, but its letters run in the wrong order.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparta was a leading city-state of ancient Greece, famed for its soldiers.

clue.text: Diana's bloomer will result in catastrophe

parts.note: Di is short for Diana, so Di's
an aster is a flower, something that blooms

explanation.surface: Diana's blunder will end in calamity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a mistake but means a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A disaster is a calamity, a sudden great misfortune.

clue.text: Also a V.I.P.

parts.note: a swell is a grand or important person

explanation.surface: Another very important person too.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-word phrase means additionally or too.
